mentions.text: BREAKING: Volkswagen is reportedly planning to cut 100,000 jobs and end production at four German plants over the coming years

The plan would see Europe’s largest automobile manufacturer shed roughly 15% of its workforce as it seeks to counter intensifying competition from Chinese car brands.

Read more: https://t.co/6Mh3vA3q7g

VOLKSWAGEN CEO OLIVER BLUME JUST OUTLINED A PLAN TO CUT UP TO 50,000 MORE JOBS AT EUROPE'S BIGGEST CARMAKER

That's on top of a similar round already underway from 2024, so as many as 100,000 positions in total.

The reason, per an internal memo seen by Bloomberg:

VW's overhead is running about one-fifth higher than competitors. Blume called reaching parity a "theoretical deduction" of roughly 50,000 jobs.

"Group headcount has been growing for decades to a level that's no longer viable today," Blume said, citing market shifts and negative effects "in the region of double-digit billion euro amounts."

Four German plants are reportedly on the table for closure: Emden, Hanover, Zwickau, and Neckarsulm. Blume says he'd rather find "smarter options" than shut them, and pointed to a 20% improvement in German factory costs over the past year.

But he also admitted the company "can't confirm a competitive allocation for the plants" right now.

Labor unions already torpedoed an earlier version of this plan and the board hasn't signed off yet.

reasons: may need to cut about 50,000 more jobs to match the competitiveness of rivals
